question: My landlord wants 15% more rent when I renew. I pay AED 80,000 a year and the rental index average for similar flats is AED 100,000. Is he allowed?

working: Shortfall = (AED 100,000 - AED 80,000) / AED 100,000 = 20.0% below the average
Decree 43/2013 Art. 1(b) applies -> maximum increase 5%
Maximum increase = 5% x AED 80,000 = AED 4,000 (new rent at most AED 84,000)
Requested 15% EXCEEDS the 5% cap
tool.rule: Decree 43/2013 Art. 1: no increase up to 10% below average; 5% for 11-20%; 10% for 21-30%; 15% for 31-40%; 20% for more than 40% below.

sources.instrument: Law No. 26 of 2007 (as amended by Law No. 33 of 2008)

caveats: The 'average rental value of similar units' is the official Rent Index figure for your unit (DLD Smart Rental Index since 2 January 2025), not a figure you estimate.
Any change must also be notified at least 90 days before the contract expires (Law 26/2007 Art. 14, as amended), unless agreed otherwise.
